newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia anthrax outbreak said under control.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia anthrax outbreak said under control.

text.p: The outbreak of cattle anthrax in the Australian state of Voctoria spread slightly in the past 24 hours but appeared to be under control after a massive vaccination programme, Peter McLaughlin, spokesman for the state's Department of Natural Resources and Environment, said.
Three more properties had been found to be infected, bringing the total to 37, while five more cattle had died, bringing the total to 77, he said on Thursday.
But a massive vaccination programme was accelerating, with 45 properties and 2,000 cattle vaccinated on Tuesday afternoon, bringing the total to 141 and 11,000 respectively, he said.
The vaccination programme would continue, he said.
The anthrax outbreak was not spreading, contrary to a Sydney newspaper report that the disease had jumped the state border into New South Wales (NSW), he said.
Victoria's anthrax outbreak was still confined to an area of about 20 km by six km, he said.
The NSW Agriculture Department's chief veterinary officer, Dick Jane, confirmed that there had been no spread of the disease from Victoria into NSW.
The six confirmed cases of anthrax in NSW cattle and sheep since last September were in the normal range expected each summer and had been dealt with without further trouble, he said.

The Australian dairy industry, meanwhile, is moving to attempt to convince Japanese consumers they have nothing to fear from Australian dairy products, sold to Japan mainly in the form of powdered milk.
The Australian Dairy Corp (ADC) would reassure Japanese consumers that it was impossible to contract anthrax from processed dairy products, trade sources said.
The ADC was unable to immediately discuss its strategies in Japan.
Japanese trading house sources said a reaction from the Japanese market was expected very soon.
"Based on past experience with food scares (in Japan), for example E. coli, it's just amazing how they react," one trading house official said.
The E. coli bacterial infection in Japan and the outbreak of "Mad Cow" disease in Britain last year caused a major drop in meat purchases in Japan last year.
Exporters of Australian dairy products are wondering whether to alert Japanese customers in advance about the anthrax situation or to wait until inquiries were received, the official said.
Asia is Australia's main market for dairy product exports, forecast to total A$1.8 billion in 1996/97, with Japan the main Asian customer. The products are exported around the world.
Anthrax is a bacterial infection which causes rapid death in cattle, sheep and goats which eat contaminated material.
It is very occasionally caught by people, mainly through scratches and the like.
